reviews.title: Something's broken - iPad OneDrive not uploading to cloud
reviews.text:
I'm a long-time user of OneDrive on PC and IOS. In attempting to upload some new files to OneDrive from my iPad, a handful got uploaded but many did not. Yes, I gave it plenty of time on a reliable WiFi connection plugged-into power. Yes, I verified file names are OK. Used to work fine, now it just stops. My frustration is that there is NO status info available (that I can find) that shows which files have been uploaded and which have not. It was not until I went to use those files on a PC that I discovered they had not made it. Very concerning, as this used to work well. At this moment, I DO NOT RECOMMEND this app on iPad as it's seriously broken.

Update: 10/31/2026
Again, another OneDrive update and they broke the app again; now, any attempt to copy a file from OneDrive to my iPad gets corrupted and can not be opened on the iPad, AND can no longer be opened or used from OneDrive. Will someone at Microsoft PLEASE test basic functionality before releasing an update.

reviews.title: Beware! Massive data lost 700GB
reviews.text:
Terrible service, I do not recommend it at all. I subscribed to the Premium plan trusting that my data would be secure, and it has been a total scam. After updating my laptop to Windows 11, OneDrive's automatic synchronization system glitched and sent my folders to the recycle bin.
The worst part came when I tried using their official "Restore your OneDrive" tool to a safe date (October 18th). The system did the exact opposite of what it was supposed to do; it misinterpreted everything and instead of recovering my files, it drastically reduced my data from 192 GB to just 96 GB right in front of my eyes. It swallowed half of my information (a total of 700 GB of actual data lost) and left my folders completely empty or incomplete!
To make matters worse, their so-called "premium technical support" is an absolute lie. They force you to chat with an incompetent, automated robot that is incapable of understanding your concerns, running you in circles only to finally give you the sole option of sending an email and sitting around for days waiting for a response that never comes. It is unacceptable for a multi-billion dollar company to destroy the information of paying customers and not have actual human staff to handle emergencies. I am canceling my subscription immediately. If you value your files and your peace of mind, stay away from this service.

reviews.title: OneDrive’s iOS File Provider authentication is broken
reviews.text:
OneDrive on iOS has become unreliable for a core function: saving files.

The OneDrive app itself can be signed in and browse files normally, while the iOS Files integration and Share Sheet simultaneously report “Sign-in required.” Tapping Sign In inside OneDrive succeeds, but the File Provider extension remains unauthenticated. Files saved to OneDrive then sit indefinitely at “Waiting…” with a cloud-outline icon and never upload.

I have reset the account, removed/re-added OneDrive in Files, restarted the phone, deleted and reinstalled OneDrive, and reauthenticated. The failure returns.

This looks like broken credential/token propagation between the main OneDrive app and its iOS File Provider/Share extensions.

Please stop treating this as a generic “sign in again” problem. Instrument the File Provider authentication flow, reproduce the stale-token state, and fix the extension/session handoff.

Cloud storage that silently fails to upload files is a data-integrity problem, not a cosmetic bug.

reviews.title: Total Joke Shame on you Microsoft
reviews.text:
This app is a complete failure.

I can sign into my Microsoft OneDrive account on a browser, my Windows PC, and my Mac with zero issues. But on iPhone, it suddenly claims my account doesn’t exist — which is beyond broken.

I even went through the “forgot username” process. It finds my account, shows it to me, I enter it exactly the same… and it still says the account doesn’t exist. That’s not user error — that’s a fundamental flaw in the app.

My login works everywhere else. Every other service accepts it instantly. So this is clearly a problem with Microsoft OneDrive on iOS.

An app that can’t even handle basic sign-in is not fit for purpose. It’s unreliable, frustrating, and frankly unacceptable — especially from a company like Microsoft.

Until this is fixed, the app is effectively unusable.

reviews.title: Almost lost for words
reviews.text:
I’ve been using Onedrive and Onenote across Windows, iPad and Android for several years. Now ditching both as MS have clearly lost the plot and neither are fit for purpose any more.

Tried accessing Onedrive today. As usual now, I get multiple prompts to log in (remember me does nothing). Log in on web, see one thing, then it opens the app, login prompt, spinning wheel, spinning wheel, “An Error has occurred. Give your administrator the following error details (codes only. No clue as to the actual error)” …. Er, who?, what?

Then it opens an item, go back to the folder, “you need to login to see these items”, login doesn’t work, it shows me the items anyway. Some don’t open.

Etc etc.

A completely unusable cluster f. May be they should stop dicking around with AI and make sure existing stuff works before trying to convince us we can trust them with anything more.

Has no one at MS worked out why their attempts to compete on cutting edge stuff keep falling short? 
 
(FWIW, I’ve worked as a tech. -> CTO and CIO and now consultant from pre Windows days onwards (often working closely with MS and contributing to their publications). I’ve used Macs since ‘84, but currently have Windows PCs. I hold no brand allegiances or bias).

reviews.title: Lost faith in Microsoft
reviews.text: Something terrible has happened to OneDrive. It used to be an easy to use and rock-solid cloud storage service for iOS devices, but over the last year several key features have broken and have not been fixed. Examples: try renaming a file. It doesn’t rename, and if you browse to it under the old filename it says “0 kB” and won’t open. However, if you search under the new name, you will see it (listed with the old name) and can open it from the search list. Another bug is when you save an email attachment to OneDrive, it saves two files, one with the name you gave it (which won’t open) and another with a date and time stamp (which will open). If you delete one, it deletes them both. It appears that it may be fixed now, but it took a year for MS to address it. I can only conclude that MS’s products for iOS have a low priority, or that MS has simply become another overgrown, poorly performing bureaucracy.
